summary.title: How to make mistakes in Python
summary.one_liner: A tour of common Python programming mistakes, from environment setup and silly typos to style and structure errors, with suggested habits to avoid them.
takeaways: Use virtual environments so that project dependencies do not conflict in the system Python.
Prefer IPython or Jupyter Notebook over the plain Python REPL for editing and exploring code.
Watch for forgotten return statements, which silently produce None, and write the return first.
Use an editor with auto-completion, write tests early, and run Pylint to catch misspellings and unused variables.
Avoid Hungarian notation and follow PEP-8 for naming and indentation.
summary.summary: The author, a Python programmer since 2000, catalogs his own mistakes in categories: setup, silly things, style, structure, and surprises. The setup chapter explains why installing packages into the system site-packages causes dependency conflicts and recommends virtualenv or pyvenv, and it suggests IPython or Jupyter over the default shell. The silly-mistakes chapter covers forgotten return values (which yield None), misspellings that tools like Pylint can flag, and confusing def/class typos. The style chapter critiques Hungarian notation and PEP-8 violations. The page is written as a personal, anecdotal essay with code examples, written for Python 2 with notes on Python 3.
